01

1.1 Our mission

To bring traditional South Indian home décor into every home, with the best value, the latest designs and a fine finish, while giving women a livelihood with dignity.

Drawn from the 2024 brand guide. Confirm the wording with the Archana Creations team.

Our vision

To be the world’s favourite destination for traditional South Indian home décor.

1.2 Who we are

Tradition, handcrafted since 1994.

Archana Creations started in 1994 in Bengaluru. We make cloth haras (garlands), torans (buntings), tomalas, dindus and other South Indian home décor. We are more than a company: a livelihood for more than 200 women.

02

2.1 Primary logo

Anatomy of the logo

  1. 1 Golden “a” — the letter A drawn as a paisley, in Archana Gold
  2. 2 Mango motif — the red paisley found in haras, rangolis and silks
  3. 3 Green curl — the fresh mango leaf of a toran
  4. 4 Spiral — a kolam line, creativity unfolding
  5. 5 Diya on a lotus — light and devotion, the meaning of archana
  6. 6 Archana Creations — Century Schoolbook Bold, in Kumkum Red
  7. 7 “Inspiring Creativity” — the tagline in script, in Archana Green
1234567

Always use the supplied file. Never redraw, recolour or rearrange it.

2.2 Logo system

One logo, four versions

The primary logo and the logomark (emblem) are from the 2024 guide. The horizontal version and the badge are new, cut from the same file — approve them before use.

1  Primary logo

The default. Website, posters, catalogues, store sign.

2  Horizontal

Wide, short spaces. Website header, letterheads, banners.

3  Logomark

When the name is already nearby. Watermarks, tags, labels.

4  Badge

Profile picture, WhatsApp, stickers, favicon.

2.3 Clear space and size

Give it room to breathe

Clear space on every side equals x, the height of the “A” in Archana. With a partner logo, follow the 2024 collaboration rule: x outside, x/2 between the two logos, and a thin divider line. Scale the logo as one piece.

xxxx

Primary

120 px · 30 mm

Horizontal

160 px · 40 mm

Badge

48 px · 12 mm

2.4 Logo on colour

Light grounds first

White, Cream and Sandal let the gold, red and green all show. On Archana Green the green curl disappears, so use the badge or a white panel. Never directly on dark teal or busy photos.

3.1 Primary colour

Archana Green

The green of the 2024 brand guide and of the logo’s mango leaf. It is our ground colour: covers, offer posts, packaging and the store strip.

3.4 Gradient

The festive gradient

Archana Green to Torana Green, like leaves in light. Cream or gold text on it. Keep red and gold as flat colours.

#006E36#157949

Buttons and bars

“Shop now” and “WhatsApp to order” pills, footer strips.

Covers and offer posts

Section openers, festive offer posts, banners.

Never red to gold

Keep red and gold flat, never blended.

3.5 Colour rules

The 60–30–10 rule

60% light — white, Cream or Sandal, so products and the logo breathe.

30% green — Archana Green panels, strips and offer posts.

10% accent — gold or red for the price, the offer or the one thing to remember.

05

5.1 Pattern

Torana and rangoli

Two motifs from the products themselves: a torana of mango leaves and marigolds, and rangoli flowers in the logo colours.

Torana at the top of posters, catalogues, signboards and reel frames, like a real toran over a door.

Rangoli as texture for backgrounds, packaging and festive greetings, on Cream or Sandal.

Keep it behind, never on top of text, prices, product photos or the logo.

Section 06

Voice

  • 6.1Brand personality
  • 6.2Tone in practice

06

6.1 Brand personality

A warm elder who knows every festival

Devotional, proud of the craft and generous with ideas. Never loud, never cheap.

Rooted

Do: Use the real names: hara, toran, tomala, rangoli.

Not: Generic words like “decoration items”.

Warm

Do: Speak like family welcoming guests home.

Not: Pushy “hurry, last stock!!!” pressure.

Proud of the craft

Do: Mention handwork, women artisans and laser finish.

Not: Hiding who makes the products.

Clear on offers

Do: Dates, discount and exclusions in one place.

Not: Offers without dates or terms.

6.2 Tone in practice

How we write

Festival or occasion first, then the product, then the offer.

English and Kannada both welcome. One or two emoji per caption at most: 🪔 🌼

Always Archana Creations — never “Archana Creation” or “Archana Collections”.

Write this

Welcome Lakshmi home this Deepavali with a hand-made toran.

Made by our women artisans in Bengaluru.

FLAT 10% OFF, 2–10 November. Not on haras, torans and tomalas.

Not this

CHEAPEST DECORATION IN BANGALORE!!!

Hurry, offer ending, buy now buy now!

All type items available. DM for price.
